name: datafusion
readiness_tier: Tier 1: High Contribution Readiness (Documented + Active Starter Tasks)
problem_statement: Modern big data workloads require lightning-fast, extensible SQL query processing that can seamlessly integrate into various data pipelines without the overhead of heavy distributed clusters. Existing traditional engines often lack modularity and native integration with the Apache Arrow memory model, limiting performance and embedding capabilities. DataFusion solves this by providing an extensible, high-performance query engine in Rust that allows developers to build custom data systems leveraging vectorization and zero-copy data sharing.
what_you_will_learn: Contributors will master advanced query optimizer design, vectorized execution engine implementation using Apache Arrow, and robust modular Rust architecture patterns for high-throughput data processing systems.
why_it_fits_complexity: It provides well-scoped modular components and clear trait-based abstractions that allow new contributors to tackle localized optimization rules or expression evaluations without needing to understand the entire engine lifecycle at once.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository, run the comprehensive test suite with `cargo test`, and explore the `good-first-issue` labels in the tracker.

name: pixi
description: Powerful system-level package manager for Linux, macOS and Windows written in Rust – building on top of the Conda ecosystem.
readiness_tier: Tier 1: High Contribution Readiness (Documented + Active Starter Tasks)
problem_statement: Managing complex cross-platform environments with binary dependencies often leads to slow resolution times, platform fragmentation, and inconsistent developer setups. Traditional tools can struggle with performance and lack modern multi-language, multi-platform package orchestration out-of-the-box. Pixi bridges this gap by offering an ultra-fast, conda-backed package and project manager written in Rust, ensuring deterministic and reproducible environments across Linux, macOS, and Windows.
what_you_will_learn: Contributors will learn advanced package management algorithms, integration with the Conda ecosystem standards, and how to build high-performance command-line interfaces in Rust with robust concurrency.
why_it_fits_complexity: The codebase features clear separation of concerns between lockfile resolution, CLI interaction, and environment manipulation, making it approachable for developers learning complex state management.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository, read the `CONTRIBUTING.md` guide, and try running the CLI tests locally using `cargo test`.

name: pyrefly
description: A fast type checker and language server for Python
readiness_tier: Tier 1: High Contribution Readiness (Documented + Active Starter Tasks)
problem_statement: Large-scale Python codebases suffer from slow static analysis and type checking, which can severely bottleneck developer velocity in massive monorepos. Existing type checkers can struggle to scale or lack responsive Language Server Protocol (LSP) integrations needed for real-time IDE feedback. Pyrefly solves this by delivering an extremely fast type checker and language server written in Rust, ensuring sub-second feedback loops for Python developers.
what_you_will_learn: Contributors will gain deep insights into compiler design, incremental computation strategies, and the implementation of the Language Server Protocol (LSP) for modern developer tooling.
why_it_fits_complexity: It isolates parsing, type inference, and server communication into distinct modules, allowing newcomers to focus on individual AST transformations or diagnostic rules.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository, inspect the test workspace, and run `cargo test` to verify your local build environment functions correctly.

name: mcfly
description: Fly through your shell history. Great Scott!
problem_statement: Standard shell history tools search linearly or rely on rudimentary keyword matching, making it frustratingly difficult to find previously executed complex commands in context. Existing alternatives often ignore critical environmental context like the current directory, exit status, and recent command frequency. Mcfly intelligently replaces the default Ctrl+R history search with a neural-backed, context-aware suggestion engine that surfaces the right command instantly.
what_you_will_learn: Contributors will learn how to interact with shell line editors, implement SQLite-based local storage engines in Rust, and apply lightweight heuristic ranking algorithms.
why_it_fits_complexity: The project has a compact, focused scope centered around database interaction, shell integration scripts, and a clean command-line interface.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository, read through the setup instructions in the README, and run the test suite using `cargo test`.

name: koharu
description: ML-powered manga translator, written in Rust.
readiness_tier: Tier 1: High Contribution Readiness (Documented + Active Starter Tasks)
problem_statement: Translating manga manually is a laborious process that requires tedious text detection, OCR, inpainting, and machine translation across complex image layouts. Existing pipelines are often fragmented, script-heavy, and difficult to deploy as cohesive standalone desktop applications. Koharu solves this by providing an all-in-one, GPU-accelerated, ML-powered manga translation desktop suite written natively in Rust.
what_you_will_learn: Contributors will explore computer vision pipeline orchestration, GUI development in Rust, and integration of deep learning runtimes for multimodal image processing.
why_it_fits_complexity: It cleanly separates heavy inference tasks from user interface event loops, making it easy to isolate and contribute improvements to specific pipeline stages.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository, examine the project architecture outlined in the documentation, and verify the build setup with `cargo check`.

name: Daft
description: High-performance data engine for AI and multimodal workloads. Process images, audio, video, and structured data at any scale
readiness_tier: Tier 1: High Contribution Readiness (Documented + Active Starter Tasks)
problem_statement: Modern AI workloads require processing petabytes of multimodal data (images, video, audio, and text) alongside structured tables, but traditional big data engines were built solely for text and tabular formats. Legacy frameworks suffer from high memory overhead and slow transformation speeds when dealing with raw unstructured data tensors. Daft solves this by offering a high-performance, Apache Arrow-native distributed data engine specifically optimized for AI and multimodal pipelines.
what_you_will_learn: Contributors will gain mastery over distributed query planning, zero-copy memory management with Apache Arrow, and execution strategies optimized for machine learning workflows.
why_it_fits_complexity: The project maintains modular abstraction layers separating the Python frontend, execution planner, and Rust compute kernel, allowing for targeted feature contributions.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository, review the contribution guidelines, and execute the core test suite to ensure your development environment is fully operational.

name: grin
description: Minimal implementation of the Mimblewimble protocol.
readiness_tier: Tier 1: High Contribution Readiness (Documented + Active Starter Tasks)
problem_statement: Cryptocurrencies often struggle with severe blockchain bloat, where historical transaction records grow indefinitely and compromise network decentralization and privacy. Traditional protocols expose transaction amounts and participant addresses on the public ledger. Grin solves this by implementing the Mimblewimble protocol, enabling highly scalable, confidential transactions through revolutionary cryptographic pruning and zero-knowledge proofs.
what_you_will_learn: Contributors will dive deep into applied cryptography, cryptographic accumulators, peer-to-peer networking protocols, and blockchain consensus mechanisms implemented in safe systems languages.
why_it_fits_complexity: It features a rigorous, academic-backed protocol implementation with well-defined cryptographic primitives, offering clear boundaries for consensus and networking logic.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository, read the architectural documentation regarding the Mimblewimble spec, and run `cargo test` to validate the core crypto libraries.

name: sail
description: Drop-in Apache Spark replacement written in Rust, unifying batch processing, stream processing, and compute-intensive AI workloads.
readiness_tier: Tier 1: High Contribution Readiness (Documented + Active Starter Tasks)
problem_statement: Organizations heavily invested in the Apache Spark ecosystem often face performance ceilings and high infrastructure costs when scaling to massive, compute-intensive AI workloads. Rewriting existing Spark pipelines into alternative systems is prohibitively expensive and disrupts existing data architectures. Sail solves this by providing a drop-in Apache Spark replacement written in Rust, unifying batch processing, stream processing, and AI workloads on top of Apache Arrow and Lakehouse standards.
what_you_will_learn: Contributors will learn distributed query execution engines, PySpark API compatibility layers, and deep interoperability techniques between Rust data primitives and Python runtimes.
why_it_fits_complexity: The codebase is structured around well-defined translation layers and execution backends, enabling developers to contribute to specific DataFrame operations or expression parsers.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository, review the contribution guidelines, and run the existing unit and integration test suites using Cargo.

name: roapi
description: Create full-fledged APIs for slowly moving datasets without writing a single line of code.
problem_statement: Exposing slowly moving datasets via instant, high-performance APIs typically requires boilerplate CRUD code and database infrastructure management. Roapi solves this by spinning up read-only REST and GraphQL APIs directly over flat files and object storage without writing any code. It eliminates the friction of traditional backend setup by leveraging Apache Arrow and DataFusion for blazing-fast columnar in-memory query execution.
what_you_will_learn: Contributors will learn how to build zero-code data APIs, leverage Apache Arrow for zero-copy memory layouts, and integrate Apache DataFusion for distributed SQL query engine execution in Rust.
why_it_fits_complexity: It provides a clear, modular structure isolating data source providers from API transport layers, making it approachable for beginners to grasp modern data engineering pipelines.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository, ensure you have Rust installed, and run cargo test to verify the test suite passes on your local machine.

name: zebar
description: Zebar is a tool for creating customizable and cross-platform taskbars, desktop widgets, and popups.
readiness_tier: Tier 1: High Contribution Readiness (Documented + Active Starter Tasks)
problem_statement: Customizing desktop environments, taskbars, and widgets across different operating systems often requires fragmented, platform-specific tooling with steep configuration curves. Zebar addresses this by providing a unified, extensible platform for rendering desktop widgets and taskbars using web technologies or native UI frameworks. It bridges the gap between aesthetic customization and performance by offloading heavy lifting to Rust.
what_you_will_learn: Developers will gain experience in cross-platform desktop UI development, event-driven architecture, and integrating web view runtimes with native system APIs.
why_it_fits_complexity: The codebase is cleanly divided into clear module boundaries separating system data providers from UI rendering layers, making isolated contributions straightforward.
suggested_first_step: Read through the CONTRIBUTING.md file and inspect the open issues tagged as good first issues.

name: miette
description: Fancy extension for std::error::Error with pretty, detailed diagnostic printing.
problem_statement: Standard error reporting in systems programming languages often lacks rich context, visual source code snippets, and actionable remediation advice. Miette solves this by offering a drop-in diagnostic extension for standard Rust errors that produces visually stunning, compiler-grade error reports complete with pointers and labels. It empowers developers to build command-line tools and parsers that communicate failures with exceptional clarity.
what_you_will_learn: Contributors will master advanced trait design in Rust, procedural macro implementation, and sophisticated string formatting techniques for terminal diagnostics.
why_it_fits_complexity: It has a focused scope centered around error formatting traits and macros, allowing newcomers to understand core Rust trait mechanics without getting lost in deep infrastructure.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository and run cargo run --example to see the various fancy error reporting styles in action.

problem_statement: Traditional ORMs either sacrifice asynchronous performance or lack the dynamic SQL generation capabilities required for complex enterprise applications. RBatis bridges this gap by providing a compile-time, asynchronous, dynamic SQL ORM tailored for Rust inspired by popular ecosystem patterns like MyBatis-Plus. It allows developers to write safe, maintainable database interactions without compromising on raw async throughput.
what_you_will_learn: Contributors will learn asynchronous database driver integration, macro-driven code generation, and query building abstractions in Rust.
why_it_fits_complexity: The clear separation between macro parsing logic and runtime database execution handlers provides well-defined boundaries for introductory contributions.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository, set up a local test database instance specified in the docs, and run the integration test suite.

description: Solving i18n for client-side and resource-constrained environments.
readiness_tier: Tier 1: High Contribution Readiness (Documented + Active Starter Tasks)

name: icu4x
description: Solving i18n for client-side and resource-constrained environments.
readiness_tier: Tier 1: High Contribution Readiness (Documented + Active Starter Tasks)
problem_statement: Traditional internationalization (i18n) libraries are often too bloated and memory-intensive for embedded systems, WebAssembly, and resource-constrained client devices. ICU4X reimagines internationalization libraries from the ground up in Rust to be modular, lightweight, and performant. It ensures software can accurately handle dates, times, numbers, and text across global locales with minimal binary size footprints.
what_you_will_learn: Developers will learn zero-allocation data parsing strategies, Unicode standards implementation, and design patterns for extremely modular library architectures.
why_it_fits_complexity: Despite dealing with complex specifications, the codebase is meticulously documented and broken down into independent data provider crates ideal for targeted contributions.
suggested_first_step: Explore the project documentation, read the architecture overview, and run cargo test within a specific component crate.

name: starcoin
description: Starcoin - A Move smart contract blockchain network that scales by layering
readiness_tier: Tier 1: High Contribution Readiness (Documented + Active Starter Tasks)
problem_statement: Early blockchain architectures struggle with scalability and secure smart contract execution due to asset-loss vulnerabilities inherent in traditional account-based models. Starcoin solves this by implementing a layered blockchain network powered by the resource-oriented Move smart contract language. It provides a secure, flexible foundation for decentralized applications with native multi-layer scaling.
what_you_will_learn: Contributors will gain hands-on insights into blockchain state management, cryptographic primitives, and peer-to-peer networking principles implemented in Rust.
why_it_fits_complexity: Its modular component design allows developers to explore utility crates and helper functions without needing to master the entire consensus engine immediately.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository and run the unit test suite to verify your build environment is fully functional.

name: jumpy
description: Tactical 2D shooter in fishy pixels style. Made with Rust-lang 🦀 and Bevy 🪶
problem_statement: Building modern, extensible 2D games with high-performance physics and modding support often requires writing complex engine glue code from scratch. Jumpy solves this by combining the data-driven Bevy game engine with Lua scripting for modding in a fast-paced 2D tactical shooter. It showcases how to structure a complete, production-ready game codebase using modern Entity Component System (ECS) architecture.
what_you_will_learn: Developers will learn Entity Component System (ECS) design patterns, game loop synchronization, and embedding scripting languages like Lua into a Rust application.
why_it_fits_complexity: The game logic is broken down into clean Bevy plugins and systems, making it approachable for contributors looking to add minor gameplay features or fix bugs.
suggested_first_step: Clone the repository, install the required system dependencies for Bevy, and run cargo run to launch the game locally.
